claims.claim: Counts may be truncated to {0,1,2} without losing any information relevant to level-3 restoration.
claims.evidence: Let h(r)=min(2,r). If a+b≤1, saturation changes neither summand nor sum; if a+b≥2, both h(a+b) and min(2,h(a)+h(b)) equal 2. For products, ab=0, ab=1, and ab≥2 respectively force both sides of h(ab)=min(2,h(a)h(b)) to be 0, 1, and 2. Thus h is a homomorphism from nonnegative-integer addition and multiplication to the saturated semiring. Transfer counts use only sums and products of nonnegative counts, while all uniqueness tests distinguish exactly zero, one, and at least two, so saturation loses no relevant information.
claims.witness: The complete algebraic case split is a+b≤1 versus a+b≥2 and ab=0, ab=1, versus ab≥2; the checker additionally verified both identities on all 16,641 ordered pairs in {0,…,128}².
claims.search_method: Proved both homomorphism identities by exhaustive symbolic cases, traced both counting lifts for any operation that could require unsaturated magnitudes or cancellation, and ran an integer-only finite check.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is decidable in O(m n^3) time under the source paper’s complexity convention.
claims.evidence: For fixed type-3 and type-2 digits, the saturated 2×2 local matrix A_i counts type-1 fillings by incoming and outgoing carry. Induction on columns proves that q_i=q_{i-1}A_i is exactly the saturated distribution of type-1 prefixes over the two carries. For fixed type-3 digits, a second induction shows that the 9-coordinate state d_i counts type-2 prefixes according to their resulting q-state; its terminal sum over q with q(alpha)=1 is one exactly for the nested predicate ∃!v2:∃!v1. Type-3 tuples then label ordinary existential reachability transitions. There are 9 q-states and 3^9 d-states, both absolute constants. Since a column has three cells, enumerating all local choices across the three types costs at most n^3 per column, establishing O(m n^3) under the stated convention.
claims.witness: An independently implemented literal evaluator and lifted evaluator agreed on all 250 one-column base-2, 31,250 two-column base-2, and 432 one-column base-3 level-3 instances, for 31,932 exact comparisons with no mismatch.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the nested quantifier semantics from the source, proved both prefix-count invariants including initial carry 0 and prescribed final carry alpha, checked empty type groups and competing carry paths, derived the state and time bounds, and exhaustively compared against literal enumeration on finite families.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is formally P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, but this vacuous completeness convention does not provide the requested matching hardness classification.
claims.evidence: Membership in P follows from claim 1. The language is nontrivial under the source semantics: in base 2, with one internal column and final carry 0, [type-3 x]+0=0 is YES via x=0, whereas [type-3 x]+1=0 is NO because x=0 gives the wrong result digit and x=1 produces final carry 1. Empty type-1 and type-2 blocks each have one empty assignment, so the nested uniqueness quantifiers behave as required. For any L in P, deciding membership in L and outputting these fixed YES/NO instances is a polynomial-time many-one reduction. Hence the formal completeness assertion is correct, while also being vacuous for every nontrivial language in P and supplying no conventional restrictive-reduction hardness classification.
claims.witness: The checker literally and through the transfer construction verified the stated fixed base-2 YES and NO instances.
claims.search_method: Checked the fixed instances against the source’s digit and carry semantics, handled the empty-quantifier case explicitly, and verified the direction and running time of the generic many-one reduction.

claims.claim: The same construction places every fixed-level additive restoration problem in P.
claims.evidence: Inductively, suppose the lower-level predicate is represented by a deterministic width-N layered state system. Eliminating the next unique type replaces a state by its vector in {0,1,2}^N of saturated counts of assignments ending in each lower state. Local updates are determined by saturated sums over that type’s digit tuples, and acceptance tests whether the saturated count over accepting lower states is exactly one. This proves the nested-uniqueness semantics and gives at most 3^N lifted states. Starting with N_0=2 carry states and applying the lift for each inner type yields a finite level-dependent tower independent of m and n. For each fixed level, the outer existential type is handled by reachability, while all local types together occupy only three cells and therefore require at most n^3 local tuples per column under the same convention. The resulting algorithm is polynomial for every fixed level.
claims.witness: The generic integer-only repeated-lift checker matched literal nested-quantifier evaluation exhaustively for every one-column base-2 instance at levels 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, as well as every tested two-column level-3 instance.
claims.search_method: Proved the repeated-lift invariant by induction on eliminated types and columns, checked the fixed-level versus input-level quantifier distinction, and exercised the generic construction through five levels using exact enumeration.

target_evidence: The exact target requires both a complete upper bound and a matching hardness classification. The draft rigorously establishes the polynomial-time upper bound for level 3, and indeed for every fixed level. Its polynomial-time-many-one P-completeness observation is formally correct but cannot serve as the requested matching hardness result because the reduction decides the source language and therefore makes every nontrivial language in P complete under that convention. No logspace or comparably meaningful restrictive-reduction lower bound is established. The final writeup explicitly limits its conclusion to the upper-bound portion and labels the resolution PARTIAL, so it neither overclaims target coverage nor understates what was proved.
checks_performed: Read only the designated source JSON and iteration-2 draft, apart from the independently created checker; did not access the web, retrieval data, receipts, prior runs, reports, or other solutions.
Read the exact target and independently classified its upper-bound and matching-hardness requirements.
Checked the source model: two addends, three independent cells per internal column, digit domain {0,…,n−1}, carry set {0,1}, initial carry 0, and prescribed terminal carry alpha.
Proved the saturated-semiring identities for all nonnegative integers and checked 16,641 finite integer pairs.
Proved the first- and second-lift prefix invariants and the exact terminal criteria for ∃v3:∃!v2:∃!v1.
Exhaustively compared literal and lifted decisions on 31,932 level-3 instances, with no mismatch.
Exhaustively compared the generic lift with literal evaluation on one-column base-2 instances at levels 1 through 5.
Verified the two-column all-type-1 example has exactly nine solutions along carry path (0,0,0) and one along (0,1,0), confirming why local uniqueness alone is insufficient.
Verified the fixed level-3 YES and NO instances used for the polynomial-time many-one completeness observation.
